subject: SLA request: EU region uptime baseline & maintenance window accounting
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@opsly.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@opsly.com
Date: 2026-08-19T09:12:00Z
Subject: SLA ask: EU region uptime baseline & maintenance carve-out

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the conversation yesterday. Opsly is evaluating Redwood for our EU-serving inference layer and we need to validate the SLA language before moving forward with the pilot. Two asks from our side:

1) For EU-hosted traffic, can Redwood accept a 99.5% monthly uptime baseline instead of 99.95%? Our infra team needs a slightly relaxed standard for the first 6 months while we migrate traffic.
2) We need scheduled maintenance windows (up to 6 hours per month) to be excluded from monthly uptime calculations and not count toward credits, provided we get advance notice.

We also want clarity on the monthly credit bands and a cap. Opsly prefers a predictable remedy: if availability dips below the baseline, a simple percentage-of-invoice credit is easier for procurement. Please see attached a short Opsly draft with our preferred wording.

Can you share a quick counterproposal and confirm whether the maintenance carve-out is acceptable with a 72-hour notice minimum? Also, please indicate whether the credit cap could be limited to 20% of monthly fees.

Thanks — if simpler, we can take a 30-minute call this week.

Best,
Marta Ruiz
Opsly — Head of Platform
Attachments: Opsly-SLA-proposal.pdf

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@opsly.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-19T14:35:00Z
Subject: Re: SLA ask: EU region uptime baseline & maintenance carve-out

Hi Marta — thanks for the outline and the draft. We’re excited about Opsly moving forward. A few points from Redwood’s side: 

• Baseline: Our standard hosted uptime commitment is 99.95% across regions. For a short-term migration accommodation we can offer a temporary regional baseline of 99.5% for up to 90 days, but only as part of a formal amendment to the SLA tied to a pilot period. We prefer to keep the long-term bar at 99.95%.

• Maintenance windows: We can accept a maintenance window exclusion but propose slightly different guardrails: maintenance must be pre-scheduled in the console and notified 72 hours in advance; total excluded scheduled maintenance can be up to 6 hours per calendar month; unscheduled emergency maintenance will not be automatically excluded.

• Credit bands (proposed):
  - Availability >= 99.95%: no credit
  - Availability >= 99.0% and < 99.95%: 5% monthly credit on affected service fees
  - Availability >= 95.0% and < 99.0%: 15% credit
  - Availability < 95.0%: 30% credit
  - Maximum aggregate monthly credit cap: 30% (we can discuss lowering this for enterprise deals)

If Opsly needs a lower cap (your ask was 20%), we can consider 20–25% for a defined period if Opsly also agrees to reserved capacity / committed monthly usage. For Dedicated or Private deployments we can have a different remedy schedule.

I attached a redline of our standard template with the above changes and a short summary table. Can we set a 30-minute alignment call on Thursday to finalize language? HubSpot deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/OPSLY-2026-004. DocuSign placeholder: https://www.docusign.com/EN/opsly-sla-draft

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Attachments: Redwood-sla-template-redline.docx

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: ben.carter@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-19T15:02:00Z
Subject: Fwd: SLA ask: EU region uptime baseline & maintenance carve-out

Ben, Kim — forwarding Opsly’s request and my counterproposal. Quick notes:

- Opsly explicitly asked to set 99.5% as the baseline for EU; I proposed a 90-day temporary baseline and kept 99.95% as the default.
- They asked for a 20% cap on credits. I signaled flexibility if they take reserved capacity.
- I proposed the 72-hour notification and pre-scheduling requirement for maintenance carve-outs.

Requesting:
- Ben: can you approve a deal-level concession to reduce the credit cap to 25% (from our proposed 30%) if Opsly commits to a 6-month pilot with a minimum committed spend? If so, we’ll offer that in writing.
- Kim: please confirm whether the proposed maintenance exclusion language (pre-scheduled in console, 72-hour notice, <=6 hours/month) is acceptable from legal and whether any additional wording is needed to avoid broad carve-outs.

Thanks — I’ll hold the Thursday slot pending your feedback.

— Naomi

On Thu, Aug 19, 2026 at 14:35 Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Marta — thanks for the outline and the draft. We’re excited about Opsly moving forward. A few points from Redwood’s side: ... (redacted)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@opsly.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-20T08:20:00Z
Subject: Re: SLA ask: EU region uptime baseline & maintenance carve-out

Hi all — quick reply after reviewing:

1) I’m comfortable approving a reduced monthly credit cap for Opsly to 25% (from our standard 30%) on the condition that Opsly:
   - Commits to a 6‑month pilot (minimum committed spend to be defined in the SOW), and
   - Agrees to reserved capacity pricing for at least 50% of pilot traffic (this gives us predictability).

2) Maintenance carve-out: I agree with Naomi’s guardrails. Additionally, please limit carve-outs to windows scheduled and accepted in the Redwood Console and require Opsly to acknowledge the scheduled window notification (we can use the console notification/confirmation as evidence).

3) Baseline: we should avoid permanently lowering the SLA baseline. Offer the temporary 90‑day baseline of 99.5% explicitly in the amendment and include an automatic revert to 99.95% unless both parties agree to extend.

If Opsly agrees to those three items I’m fine with moving forward and authorizing us to finalize the redlines. I’ve attached a short CSV that maps the credit bands for finance.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
Attachments: SLA-summary-table.csv
